judge.reasoning: The system answer perfectly explains and mathematically defines the MultiHead function, explicitly including the Concat operation as requested.

rows.answer:
Multi-head attention is computed by linearly projecting the queries, keys, and values $h$ times with different, learned linear projections, performing the attention function in parallel, concatenating the outputs, and projecting them again. Mathematically, it is defined as:

$$\text{MultiHead}(Q, K, V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, ..., \text{head}_h)W^O$$
$$\text{where } \text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)$$

where the projections are parameter matrices:
- $W_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$
- $W_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$
- $W_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}$
- $W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{h d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}$

rows.answer:
The late interaction operator, $\text{LI}(q, d)$, is computed as the sum over all query vectors $\mathbf{E}_q^{(i)}$ of their maximum dot product with each of the document embedding vectors $\mathbf{E}_d^{(j)}$. Formally, it is defined as:

$$\text{LI}(q, d) = \sum_{i \in [1, N_q]} \max_{j \in [1, N_d]} \langle \mathbf{E}_q^{(i)} | \mathbf{E}_d^{(j)} \rangle$$
